approach: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, replace `reading_text_fields` with a helper `file_bound_text_fields` that returns only the acceptance criteria whose kind is `Content`, labelled `acceptance_criteria[i]`. `check_boundary_and_repo_files` scans those and the deliverable paths with `athena_context::briefs::boundary_scan`. Title, summary, decline_reason, question, departures, hard_reason, urgent_reason, assumptions, out_of_scope, defaults_applied and `behavior` criteria are no longer scanned. The repository-file checks and the request-text scan (`scan_request_input`) are unchanged. The refusal message names "deliverable path or content acceptance criterion". The module docs (one line today), the doc comments and D153 state the scope, the reason (records are outside the policy scan; the writer has the word list, D73) and the two edge cases of using criterion kind as the signal. Rewrite the reading.rs tests that expected prose refusals. Fix the end-to-end test in run_pin_tests.rs (a departure from the reading's deliverables: it asserts a summary-only refusal and would fail), keeping the refusal end to end through a content criterion and adding a summary-accepted twin. Add four boundary-word cases to the refusal corpus (another departure, a test file only) so the narrowing is pinned in the corpus, not only in unit tests.

decisions.choice: Scan only deliverable paths and `content`-kind acceptance criteria; skip `behavior` criteria and all other prose. Criterion kind is the deciding signal.
decisions.reason: A `content` criterion describes file text, so a word there can reach a tracked file. A `behavior` criterion names commands to run. Prose in a record never reaches a scanned file, and the writer already gets the word list and runs the scan (D73). Kind is the only signal in the `Criterion` struct. It is imperfect in two ways, and D153's Tradeoff and the module docs say so: (a) a `content` criterion that describes a document without quoting text is still scanned, so it can be refused with no word reaching a file; (b) a `behavior` criterion that quotes output (for example 'prints "..."') is not scanned, so the writer could copy a word into a test. Backstops for (b): the writer's own scan (D73) and the policy scan at verification (xtask/tests/policy.rs).

rejected.option: Keep scanning every acceptance criterion and drop only the other prose fields
rejected.why: Behavior criteria are commands and checks, not file text. Scanning them still refuses readings for words that cannot reach a file, and the request and reading say content criteria only.

rejected.option: Remove the word check from readings entirely
rejected.why: A word in a deliverable path or in text a criterion tells the writer to write would reach a file and fail the policy scan at verification. The request keeps the check there.

rejected.option: Special-case the refused requests (allow-list or retry exemption)
rejected.why: The scope of the rule is wrong, so fix the scope. A per-request exception leaves the next prose-only refusal in place (root-cause default).

rejected.option: Change the boundary scan or word list in athena_context::briefs
rejected.why: Out of scope. The scan is the one the policy test runs; only where the reading check applies it changes.

decisions.choice: Keep the name and signature of `check_boundary_and_repo_files`; change only its scan set and messages.
decisions.reason: Callers (`check_reading_acceptance`, work_decisions.rs line 574) and the corpus (`Expected::Refuse("check_boundary_and_repo_files")`, case `crate-relative-deliverable-path`) name it. The diff stays small.

rejected.option: Rename it or split it into a words check and a repo-files check
rejected.why: Wider diff, breaks the corpus check name, no behavior gain.

decisions.choice: Reword the repair text to say 'deliverable path or content acceptance criterion' and assert that text in the criterion-2 test.
decisions.reason: The reader should be told which two places are scanned. 'Its text' no longer matches. A grep of *.rs and *.md found the old strings only in reading.rs.

rejected.why: It would send the reader to reword prose that is no longer the problem.

decisions.choice: Modify run_pin_tests.rs: move the word in `a_reading_with_a_boundary_word_is_not_accepted_and_the_word_reaches_the_caller` from `summary` to `acceptance_criteria[0].text` (kind `content` in the fixture, run_pin_tests.rs:175-177), assert the error names `acceptance_criteria`, and add a twin test where the word is in `summary` and `proposal.reading.is_some()`.

Keeping the refusal end to end through a content criterion shows the refused word still reaches the caller and the reader is re-briefed with it; the twin shows prose is accepted end to end.

rejected.why: It is the only test showing the refusal reaches the reader brief and is committed without a reading.

rejected.option: Leave it and rely on 'the check only narrows'
rejected.why: A narrowed check can still break a test that asserts the old refusal. It would fail criterion 5.

decisions.choice: Add four corpus cases in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs under a new input form tag `boundary-word` (INPUT_FORMS grows from 16 to 17), words built from pieces.
decisions.reason: The brief requires mapping each input form of a changed refusal rule to a corpus case. The corpus has no case for a boundary word anywhere (grep for boundary/banned found only the check name at line 516, which is a repo-path case). Without these, the corpus passes before and after the change and shows nothing.

rejected.option: Rely on the existing cases and unit tests
rejected.why: The corpus would not fail if the narrowing were missing.

demonstrations.method: No-regression check backed by a subset argument, plus new corpus cases that pin the behavior. Input forms of the rule and their corpus cases: word in a deliverable path -> new `boundary-word-in-a-deliverable-path` (Refuse `check_boundary_and_repo_files`); word in a content criterion -> new `boundary-word-in-a-content-criterion` (Refuse the same check); word in the summary -> new `boundary-word-in-the-summary` (Accept); word in an assumption -> new `boundary-word-in-an-assumption` (Accept); crate-relative deliverable path (repo-file branch, unchanged) -> existing `crate-relative-deliverable-path`; full deliverable path -> existing `full-deliverable-path`; governance, absent-file and brand-word forms -> existing `request-names-a-governance-file-the-reading-ignores`, `request-names-a-governance-file-the-reading-excludes`, `text-relies-on-an-absent-file`, `text-says-the-file-does-not-exist-yet`, `brand-word-and-placeholder-are-not-repo-paths`. The other listed forms (bullets, numbered parts, job citations, retry complaints, producer-report evidence, code survey, design) do not touch this rule and keep their cases (for example `steward-three-dash-bullets`, `retry-complaint-reading-omits-the-job`, `criterion-rests-on-the-producer-report`). The subset argument: after the change the scanned set (paths plus content criteria) is contained in the old set (all fields plus paths) and the problem list gets no new entries, so no reading is newly refused. I did not run the corpus and cite no result; the 0% is by construction and corpus, not a measured rate over past readings.
